{{Quote|There's…too many of them!|Gureni Telsij|audio=Telsij-TooMany.flac|<ref name="Episode VI" />}}
'''Gureni Telsij''' was a [[human]] who served as a [[lieutenant]] and [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. At the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]], he flew a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]] as part of [[Gray Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gray Squadron]], jumping to the [[Endor system]] in order to try and destroy the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]].

After the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] realized that it had fallen into a trap, hundreds of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] and [[TIE/IN interceptor|TIE interceptors]] attacked the rebels, causing Telsij to declare that there were too many of the enemy. Moments later, the [[pilot]] was [[Death|killed]] when his [[BTL Y-wing starfighter|Y-wing]] was hit by enemy fire.

==Biography==
[[Lieutenant]] Gureni Telsij was a [[human]] who served as a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]] in the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="RSOWM" /> He<ref name="Junior" /> flew a [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber]] as part of [[Gray Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gray Squadron]],<ref name="RSOWM" /> a mixed [[starfighter]] [[squadron]] of [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter]]s, [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]]s<ref name="SWGeek">''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]''</ref> and [[BTL Y-wing starfighter|Y-wings]]<ref name="RSOWM" /> under the [[Commanding officer|command]] of [[Gray Leader]]<ref name="Episode VI" /> [[Horton Salm]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]''</ref> In [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Death" /> the squadron flew alongside [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]], [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green Squadron]], and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] during the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet's]] [[Battle of Endor|attack]] on the Imperial [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|Death Star II]] [[superweapon]] over the [[moon]] of [[Endor]].<ref name="Episode VI" />

[[File:Telsij-StarfighterManual.png|thumb|left|300px|Gureni Telsij flew at the Battle of Endor.]]
Believing that they had the element of surprise and that the [[Death Star]]'s [[Deflector shield|shields]] were down, the [[fleet]] traveled through [[hyperspace]]<ref name="Episode VI" /> from the [[Sullust system]]<ref name="RotJ novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref> to the [[Endor system]] and prepared for an attack run on the [[battle station]]; however, after discovering that the Empire was [[Jammer|jamming]] them, Alliance [[General]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] realized that they had fallen into a trap. The general warned the rebel [[pilot]]s that the shields were still up and called off the attack run, but as the entire fleet pulled away from the [[Space station|station]], they discovered a large [[Imperial Navy|Imperial fleet]]<ref name="Episode VI" /> emerging from the far side of the moon.<ref name="OtFL">''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]''</ref>

As hundreds<ref name="RotJ novel" /> of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] and [[TIE/IN interceptor|interceptors]] engaged the Alliance pilots, Telsij declared that there were too many enemy [[Starship|ships]].<ref name="Episode VI" /> Moments later, he was [[Death|killed]] when his fighter was struck by enemy fire.<ref name="Death" /> The Alliance went on to ultimately destroy the Death Star and claim a major victory at Endor, although not without heavy casualties.<ref name="Episode VI" />

==Personality and traits==
Telsij lost hope upon seeing the large number of enemy fighters during the Battle of Endor. He had dark [[hair]] and [[eye]]s and [[Color|tan]] skin.<ref name="Episode VI" />

==Equipment==
[[File:TelsijHelmet.png|thumb|right|250px|Gureni Telsij wore a personalized flight helmet.]]
While piloting his Y-wing at Endor, Telsij wore a gray [[flight suit]], with Gray Squadron's flight suit at the [[time]] consisting of a pressurized [[Environment suit|g-suit overall]] with an [[equipment overvest]] and a pair of black [[flight glove]]s. Telsij's red, white, and yellow [[flight helmet]] was decorated with a row of slanted green lines above its fitted facetted glare visor, with the visor protecting him from [[radiation]] generated by [[star]]light, weapon fire, or explosions. It was also equipped with a connection point for a [[Breath mask|respirator]] and a built in wireless [[Comlink|communicator]] linked to his Y-wings comms package.<ref name="HC26">{{HelmetCollectionCite|26|Helmets}}</ref>

The [[helmet]] was personalized with red symbols on the top and back and a partially worn off red and white emblem on the chin,<ref name="HC26" /> the latter of which was also present on the helmets of Salm and [[Keyser Salm|Red Two]] during the Battle of Endor,<ref name="Episode VI" /> and on the helmet of a [[Weapons officer|weapons system officer]] in the squadron.<ref name="FFG">{{FFGXW2|set=Jango Fett's Slave I Expansion Pack|cardname=Weapons Systems Officer}}</ref> Other markings on Telsij's helmet included a red logo and a green pattern on the right side of the helmet.<ref name="HC26" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Filming===
[[File:RadioFreeBolinas.png|thumb|left|300px|A recreation of the "Radio Free Bolinas" logo]]
Gureni Telsij appeared in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']],<ref name="Episode VI" /> and was the first ''[[Star Wars]]'' character portrayed by an Asian actor with dialogue. According to stage director Hilary Westlake, the actor who portrayed Telsij is likely to have been [[Eiji Kusuhara]],<ref name="NPR">{{WebCite|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/codeswitch/2014/12/29/372670957/diversity-in-space-tracking-the-first-asian-pilot-in-the-star-wars-movies|text=Diversity In Space: Tracking The First Asian Pilot In The Star Wars Movies|author=Haruch, Steve|date=2014-12-14|work=[[Wikipedia:National Public Radio|National Public Radio]]|archivedate=20190518192028}}</ref> who is listed on a call sheet for the film as a "Y-Wing pilot."<ref name="Callsheet">{{WebCite|url=https://propstore.com/mobile/product/star-wars-ep-vi-return-of-the-jedi/revenge-of-the-jedi-call-sheet-40a|text=Revenge Of The Jedi Call Sheet - 40A|work=[https://propstore.com propstore.com]|archiveurl=https://archive.vn/SWFx0|archivedate=2021-11-24}}</ref> Westlake was a close friend of Kusuhara's and wrote the latter's obituary. After viewing footage of Telsij's scene, Westlake told [[Wikipedia:NPR|NPR]] that, "Albeit brief, I would say it is most certainly Eiji."<ref name="NPR" />

The Y-wing cockpit scenes for ''Return of the Jedi'' were filmed on Stage 9 at [[Elstree Studios]] between [[March 2]] and [[March 11]], [[1982]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> The footage of Telsij in the film has been mirrored<ref name="Episode VI" /> based on comparison of his helmet with behind the scenes photos of the prop. The emblem on the chin of Telsij, Salm, and Red Two's helmet is a tattered sticker from "Radio Free Bolinas," a [[Wikipedia:San Francisco Bay Area|San Francisco Bay Area]] broadcaster.<ref name="Costumes">''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref>

===Naming and errors===
[[File:Ekelarc_Yong.png|thumb|right|250px|Gureni Telsij has been misidentified as fellow pilot Ekelarc Yong (pictured) in multiple sources.]]
In the new ''Star Wars'' [[canon]], the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' first identified the character as just "Lieutenant Telsij,"<ref name="AEYNTK">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref> a name originating in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the "[[Death Star II Limited]]" set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] released by [[Decipher]] in [[2000]].<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Telsij}}</ref> The [[2019]] canon reference book ''[[Rebel Starfighters Owners' Workshop Manual]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]], then provided Telsij with the first name Gureni.<ref name="RSOWM" />

The [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] incorrectly identifies a photo of Telsij as [[Ekelarc Yong]], another Y-wing pilot seen in ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="Rebel Pilots Databank">{{Databank|rebel-pilots-biography-gallery|Rebel Pilots Biography Gallery}} {{C|Slide 15}}</ref> This error was repeated on a card released in [[2021]] in the [[Star Wars: Card Trader|''Star Wars'': Card Trader]] app.<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=2021 Base - Series 3|cardname=Lt. Ekelarc Yong}}</ref>
